title: Remote state preparation of a single-spin state via hybrid spin-photon entanglement
authors: Yunge Jiang, Yehan Yu, Lili Song, Yan Mu, Chaoyun Peng, Mingfeng Wang
abstract: Remote state preparation is a fundamental quantum-information protocol that exploits prior knowledge of a target state to reduce the communication resources required for quantum-state distribution. Here, we propose a remote-state-preparation protocol for a stationary electron-spin qubit using hybrid entanglement between the electron spin and a coherent-state light pulse, generated by spin-dependent reflection from a spin-cavity system. Unlike single-photon encodings, the coherent-state encoding is naturally tolerant of photon loss: a loss channel attenuates the coherent-state amplitude, leading to a gradual reduction in preparation fidelity rather than probabilistic protocol failure. The central difficulty---implementing the projection onto superpositions of nonorthogonal coherent states required in the conventional protocol---is circumvented by coupling the transmitted pulse to an auxiliary spin, followed by homodyne detection and a spin projective measurement. The protocol therefore avoids direct coherent-state-superposition measurements and photon-number-resolving detection. In the ideal limit, deterministic preparation of a particular class of target states can be achieved using only one bit of classical communication. We analytically quantify the effects of coherent-state nonorthogonality, fiber loss, and spin dephasing on the preparation fidelity. Increasing the coherent-state amplitude improves state distinguishability and hence the preparation fidelity, but also enhances which-branch information leakage caused by photon loss, resulting in an optimal amplitude at each transmission distance. For experimentally relevant parameters, the optimized average fidelity remains well above the classical benchmark over distances of tens of kilometers. We also discuss a possible implementation using diamond nitrogen-vacancy centers.
summary: This work proposes a robust remote state preparation protocol for a single-spin qubit by leveraging hybrid entanglement between the spin and a coherent light pulse. By employing a novel measurement scheme involving homodyne detection on the light field and a spin measurement, the protocol avoids difficult direct measurements on non-orthogonal coherent states. The results show high fidelity achievable over long distances, making it a promising tool for quantum communication networks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of remotely preparing an unknown single-spin quantum state using hybrid entanglement between an electron spin and a coherent light pulse.
main_result: The proposed protocol achieves deterministic state preparation in the ideal limit using only one bit of classical communication, with the fidelity remaining above the classical benchmark over tens of kilometers for relevant parameters.
method: The authors circumvent conventional measurement difficulties by coupling the transmitted pulse to an auxiliary spin, followed by homodyne detection and a spin projective measurement.
model_or_system: The system involves a stationary electron-spin qubit coupled to a high-finesse optical cavity, generating hybrid entanglement with a propagating coherent-state light pulse.
key_observables: RSP fidelity ($F$), Concurrence ($C$), and the coherent-state overlap ($\langle \alpha | -\alpha angle$).
important_parameters: Coherent-state amplitude ($\alpha$), fiber loss, and spin dephasing rates.
main_assumptions: The analysis considers the non-orthogonality of coherent states and models the process using a hybrid spin-photon entanglement scheme.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the RSP protocol using hybrid entanglement, details the measurement scheme involving homodyne detection and an auxiliary spin, analyzes the fidelity dependence on system parameters, and concludes by comparing results to the classical benchmark.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, loss-tolerant protocol for quantum state transfer that utilizes continuous variables (coherent states) in a solid-state platform, bridging quantum optics and quantum information theory.
